Subject: Quick ask — launch week capacity and billing path

Hi Aisha,

We're kicking off a product marketing blast for the 3-day launch starting 2026-07-10. Traffic will be unpredictable — we expect short spikes potentially 6-8x our baseline QPS during peak minutes. We don't have the budget authority to increase a long-term commit, but we need temporary headroom so the customer-facing features don't timeout.

Attached is our high-level launch plan (launch_plan_q2.pdf) and expected traffic window. Can Redwood provide a short-run "capacity lane" for the three-day window and confirm how overrun charges / reconciliation would work? Specifically:
- Provisional uplift for 72 hours and how you invoice overrun (true-up vs blended temporary rate)
- Any soft caps or throttles we should expect and whether fallbacks are supported
- Quick turnaround timing to approve (we need an answer by next Friday to lock comms)

If a narrow headroom path isn't feasible, note that we could explore a small short-term prepay. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
VP Product
Oregon Tech

Hey Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the plan. Looping in Ben (sales) for pricing, Monica (CS) for operational handoffs and runbook, and Laura (billing) for invoicing/true-up mechanics.

High-level proposal we can scope quickly:
1) Provisional headroom (72 hours): we stand up a temporary capacity lane that routes traffic to a reserved burst pool.
2) Billing: invoice a provisional uplift at a blended overrun rate, then true-up after the event against actual consumption with either a credit or invoice adjustment.
3) Safeguards: soft-cap threshold alerts and automated fallback to a cheaper model variant if the headroom is exceeded.

Ben — can you draft 1–2 pricing options (short-lived uplift + reconciliation) we can send to Samir? Monica — please confirm what operational handoffs you need. Laura — any special invoicing language for provisional charges that we should surface?

Samir — quick Q: roughly what peak QPS and total additional token volume are you budgeting for the 72-hour window? That will determine the uplift size and pricing band.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — launch week capacity and billing path

Team — drafting the pricing options for Samir. Two sensible paths depending on what's most important to them (predictability vs cost):

Option A — Provisional headroom (predictable, higher base):
- Temporary uplift allocated for 72 hours. Flat uplift fee: $5,000/day for the reserved burst pool (covers baseline GPU standing cost).
- Overrun bands after uplift exhausted: 0–20%: base hosted rate; 20–100%: base hosted rate + 15% surcharge; >100%: base hosted rate + 30% surcharge
- Post-event true-up: reconcile actual token usage vs provisional commitment, invoice differences net of any applied credits.
- If they convert uplift to a 3-month commit within 30 days, we apply a 30% credit against month 1 invoice.

Option B — Usage-first (lower upfront, variable cost):
- No flat uplift fee; allow burst pool access with an overage blended rate for the 72-hour window: base hosted rate + 10% blended premium applied to all incremental tokens during the window.
- Hard soft-cap at 10x baseline QPS to avoid runaway cost; automated fallback to cheaper variant if hit.
- Post-event true-up: one consolidated invoice for the blended incremental usage.

Notes:
- Either option includes a one-page runbook and an on-call contact from Monica's team for the window.
- We can shorten approval time by pre-issuing a provisional invoice that acts as a hold. Laura — can we pre-authorize a provisional invoice and then apply adjustments?

Ben
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

2) Choose Option A or B (Ben's note) or request a blended variant.
